hero: In a Quezon City tertiary hospital clinic, a Filipino nephrology fellow and an internal medicine resident lean over a ward microscope examining a urine sediment while a 24-year-old Filipina call-center agent in a company lanyard sits on the exam bed and her mother stands beside her; morning light, calm and attentive mood, no text.

figures.teaches: The site of glomerular injury determines whether the patient presents with a nephritic, nephrotic, mixed or rapidly progressive picture.
figures.content: Center: one glomerular capillary loop in cross-section with three labeled layers: 'Endothelium', 'Glomerular basement membrane (GBM)', 'Podocyte with foot processes'. Four numbered callouts. 1 'Inflamed capillary and mesangium' (immune deposits, neutrophils, ruptured loop, red cells escaping) -> box 'Nephritic: dysmorphic red cells, red cell casts, rising creatinine, hypertension' with examples 'IgAN, post-infectious GN, lupus III/IV'. 2 'Injured podocyte, no inflammation' (flattened foot processes, albumin passing) -> box 'Nephrotic: protein >3.5 g/day, albumin low, edema, bland sediment' with examples 'MCD, primary FSGS, membranous'. 3 'Thickened GBM with deposits' -> box 'Mixed: heavy protein plus some blood' with examples 'lupus V, diabetic kidney disease'. 4 'Crescent filling Bowman's space' -> red box 'Rapidly progressive: creatinine rising day by day; call tonight'. Muted clinical palette; red reserved for box 4.

figures.teaches: A biopsy is done when its result will change management, is prepared for safety, and is split so that all three parts of the report are possible.
figures.content: Vertical flowchart. Step 1 diamond 'Will the result change management?' No -> 'Monitor protein, BP, eGFR'; Yes -> Step 2 'Urgent? (rising creatinine, positive ANCA or anti-GBM)' -> side note 'Do not delay treatment for the biopsy'. Step 3 'Make it safe: BP controlled, platelets and clotting checked, antithrombotics held per protocol'. Step 4 'Split the tissue: light microscopy | immunofluorescence | electron microscopy; confirm where each core is sent and who pays'. Step 5 'Read the report' with three columns: 'Light: pattern + chronicity (sclerosed glomeruli, fibrosis)', 'Immunofluorescence: IgA mesangial / full house / linear IgG / pauci-immune / granular IgG', 'EM: deposit location, foot process effacement'. Footer risk strip: 'Pooled 118,064 native biopsies: transfusion 1.6%, intervention 0.3%, death 0.06%'.
